2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l62.c11/text: How the fuck did Florida tie are you fucking kidding me
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l77.c7/text:
“Too close to call!”

The state of Florida has a margin of victory under half a percent, and with the election hinging on its result, the recounts in the state are going to decide it. Every court option and legal procedure will be investigated by you and your opponent, so be ready for the long haul. Let’s hope this delay in fundamental democracy doesn't result in the unpreparedness of any critical governmental agencies. That would be truly terrible!
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l81.c6/text:
“GOD FUCKING DAMNIT GORE”

Those words rang out from the president's office, despite the door being shut. In the room, were President Bill Clinton and Vice President Al Gore.'I BROUGHT THE ECONOMY BACK FROM A TERRIBLE STATE RUN BY INCOMPETENT REPUBLICANS. I WON DURING THE MID-TERMS AND GAVE YOU A FREE TICKET TO THE PRESIDENCY. AND WHAT DO YOU DO? YOU LET THE SON OF THE GUY WHO I BEAT BECOME PRESIDENT! 538 VOTES TO 0!' Those were the words of a less than happy Bill Clinton. Gore responded 'I-I don't know what happened, I-I thought I ran a good campaign b-but...' Clinton interrupted, saying 'You know exactly what happened Gore. For some reason, you did a tank photo op like Dukakis, which is already bad enough. BUT THEN you accidentally fired the tank, I have no clue how, those things are hard to fire, and you hit a group of spectators. Killing 5. Your court date is in a month so you better start prepping a defence team.' 'co-' 'If you’re asking me for a pardon, you can shove it. Then in your speech to the nation about it, you claimed the ghost of William Mckinley had fired the tank by controlling your body. You then spent 50 thousand dollars of taxpayer money on hiring an exorcist to try and remove him. That’s why you lost, Al.
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l100.c28/text: You still have many options for your political career as of now. You are still popular in your party and Texas, so there is no doubt you can still influence the next candidate. Perhaps it will be you, or your brother. Maybe the American public will get sick of the Bush family and choose someone else entirely. Whatever the case, let’s hope the Republicans can recover as the Democrats did 8 years ago.
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l103.c31/text: Despite your best efforts, Al Gore will succeed Clinton in the presidency. Many Republicans are disappointed with your loss, seeing the Monica Lewinsky scandal, among others a real opening for them to return to the White House. The closeness of the election will likely inspire Gore to be a bit more moderate and bipartisan in his decision-making. With the close Senate, it will certainly be needed.
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l106.c31/text: Despite your best efforts, Al Gore will succeed Clinton in the presidency. Many Republicans are disappointed with your loss, seeing the Monica Lewinsky scandal, among others a real opening for them to return to the White House. Gore flipping the House and Senate will give him some breathing room, but with the slim margins, he will have his work cut out for him.
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l109.c31/text: Despite your best efforts, Al Gore will succeed Clinton in the presidency. Many Republicans are disappointed with your loss, seeing the Monica Lewinsky scandal, among others a real opening for them to return to the White House. Many are shocked at the margin you lost by, seeing the Lewinsky scandal as giving a lot of socially conservative states the impetus to vote for you. Many it really IS just the economy that matters.
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l113.c28/text: For the first time since 1888, the loser of the popular vote has won the election! This has many Republicans enraged, especially due to the fact this is the 3rd Democrat in a row winning with less than 50% of the popular vote. Maybe a run in 4 years IS in the books for you...
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l117.c28/text: What will happen next is up to you, although most people have some expectations. Tax cuts will certainly be going into effect, and some bills related to gay marriage or LGBTQ+ people in the military will as well. Just keep an eye out for 2004, and don't make the same mistakes as your dad.
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l120.c31/text: Well done! You've prevented another term of Democrats and succeeded your father as the next Republican president. Your impressive margin allows the Senate and House to stay in Republican hands, with a Republican president for the first time since Dwight Eisenhower!
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l124.c31/text: Well done! You've prevented another term of Democrats and succeeded your father as the next Republican president. You've managed to flip a few seats in the house and Senate, but it's best you act quickly on your promises or the midterms could take that all away.
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l128.c31/text: Well done! You've prevented another term of Democrats and succeeded your father as the next Republican president. You barely won, however, so let’s hope your bipartisanship and compassionate conservativism resonate with many Americans.
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l132.c29/text: For the first time since 1888, the loser of the popular vote has won the election! This has many Democrats are very angry, especially at Ralph Nader for "spoiling" the election.
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l141.c28/text: It's up to you what you want to do next. A run in 4 years isn't totally out of the question, but after your decades in politics, you might be burnt out. In any case, let’s hope Bush can continue the economic prosperity and tone down the foreign policy intervention, such as in Somalia. Anything more like that would be a disaster...
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l143.c31/text: It just seems all the little things affecting your campaign were too much to handle. Maybe you should have emphasized your relation to Clinton more. Maybe you should have moved politically left to catch some votes from Nader. Maybe you should have moved politically RIGHT to appeal to the south. Whatever it is, George Bush will be the next president. At least with the close margin, Bush's bipartisanship will have to be on full display.
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l145.c31/text: It just seems all the little things affecting your campaign were too much to handle. Maybe you should have emphasized your relation to Clinton more. Maybe you should have moved politically left to catch some votes from Nader. Maybe you should have moved politically RIGHT to appeal to the south. Whatever it is, George Bush will be the next president. As it has since 94, the House and Senate will be Republican hands firmly, as they made some small gains.
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l147.c31/text: It just seems all the little things affecting your campaign were too much to handle. Maybe you should have emphasized your relation to Clinton more. Maybe you should have moved politically left to catch some votes from Nader. Maybe you should have moved politically RIGHT to appeal to the south. Whatever it is, George Bush will be the next president. Bush won by a larger than expected amount, and as such, the Senate and House will favour him heavily. I guess his bipartisanship won't be needed for the next two years...
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l151.c29/text: For the first time in over a century, the loser of the popular vote has won the election! Your fellow Democrats are already having flashbacks of 1888, and are blaming Ralph Nader for it.
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l155.c28/text: You'll no doubt be continuing the economic policies of Clinton, but with your own, Al Gore twist. The environment, healthcare for all, and technology will be your 3 goals of the next term, and if you are successful as Clinton in your achievements, 2004 will be a cakewalk.
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l157.c31/text: Despite another challenge being thrown at you, you've cast aside George Bush and flipped the script on the Republicans, allowing Democrats to win their own 3 presidential elections in a row. Another commanding win for the Democrats as well, and with this, you have flipped both chambers back. Who cares about 1994, anyways?
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l159.c31/text: Despite another challenge being thrown at you, you've cast aside George Bush and flipped the script on the Republicans, allowing Democrats to win their own 3 presidential elections in a row. The house and Senate have tightened up in your favour, but you will still have to appeal to moderate Democrats to pass legislation.
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l162.c31/text: Despite another challenge being thrown at you, you've cast aside George Bush and flipped the script on the Republicans, allowing Democrats to win their own 3 presidential elections in a row. Unfortunately, your win was nowhere near as big as Clinton's, so the chambers are in the Republicans favour for now.
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l166.c28/text: Interestingly enough, you've lost the popular vote despite winning overall, for the first time since 1888. Republicans aren't too happy about losing 3 elections in a row to someone who won less than 50% of the popular vote.
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l174.c12/text:
”As expected, you've lost the 2000 election.”

Congratulations! You received 5% of the popular vote! You will enable the Green Party to run a vigorous campaign in 2004 and present a true choice to the American people. You’ve run a great campaign these last few months, and you should have no problem getting renominated in 4 years.

But for now, sit back and relax, you’ve earned it. Who knows? Maybe next election you’ll even win a state or two.
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l178.c12/text:
”Congratulations! You’ve won D.C.!”

What a campaign! You’ve managed to surpass expectations and net yourself some electoral votes! You should have no trouble gaining federal matching funds next election, and you can take solace in the fact that the people of D.C. chose the only capable man this election.

Democrats are sure to be miffed, especially so if they lost, but you couldn’t care less at this moment. Good luck in 2004!
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l182.c9/text:
”Holy Cow! You won a state!”

Everyone thought it impossible, but you’ve pulled it off! You’re the first third-party candidate in over 30 years to win a state, and both you and your supporters are ecstatic. Federal matching funds in 2004 are all but guaranteed, and you’ve established the green party as a force to be reckoned with.

Let’s hope you’re more than just a flash in the pan and can run a similar campaign in 2004. The Green party may even find itself in the White House someday - and it’s all thanks to you.
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l186.c12/text:
”The Senate will now vote on H.R. 5411, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2001.”

Those were the words of the clerk in the US Senate. They went through each Senator by state, asking for a voice vote from each of them. After all, was said and done, the tally was 81-19 in favour of the motion. the clerk said 'The motion passes. The bill will now be presented to the president for signing.' He stood up and turned around, only to see president Ralph Nader standing 2 inches behind him, which causes the Clerk to stumble back. 'Oh, h-hello there President Nader. I was just going to pres-' He gets interrupted by the loudest yell he had ever heard, when president Nader bellowed at him:

VETOED!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

president Nader then had his 74th veto overridden that congress just 5 minutes later.
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l190.c12/text:
”Good lord! You’ve won the 2000 election!”

Everyone thought it impossible, that at best you would get 5%, but you’ve proved everybody wrong! This is the biggest political upset in American history, beating out Truman over 50 years ago. An impromptu party has been arranged at the Green Party headquarters in DC, your answering machine is clogged with congratulatory calls from your supporters, and every news station in the country has been clamouring to get to you for an interview

What you've achieved tonight is a stellar victory that will be studied for the rest of American history. From Nader’s Raiders to the White House in 30 years, let’s hope your surprise victory has also netted the Green Party some senate seats, or you’ll have to compromise big in the coming years, considering your stiff opposition from both parties. This definitely wasn’t supposed to happen - Good luck!
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l194.c10/text:
"It is Over"

The results are coming in, and the phone is ringing. You reach slowly into your drawer and pull out something you never thought you would use. The TV announcer drawls, "The biggest loser of tonight is Ralph Nader! Nader appears to have only received
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l194.c305/text:
votes nationwide." You pull the gun to your head, and slowly press on the trigger... and then there was nothing.

A noise suddenly grabs your attention, but your vision is still fuzzy.

"Ralph, cmon!"

The voice seems strained. Your vision suddenly clears. You are in a white room. As your eyes trail sluggishly around the room, you notice something strange. There are a series of glass pods lining the sides of the room. In each pod, there is a person inside each, with every person having some form of cap on their head.

"Get out of the simulator, Ralph! We have some shopping to do," and then finally, you remembered.
2000_Gore_Bayh/ending/s0.l198.c12/text:
”As expected, you've lost the 2000 election.”

This was hardly a surprise, considering the stranglehold that the two-party system holds on American politics. To make matters worse, you didn’t even get 5% of the popular vote, so the Green Party will have to do without federal matching funds.

Still, you’ve run a decent campaign, and your campaign has tried the best it could. You have a chance to cross that 5% threshold in the next election at least, considering you’ve been a perennial candidate for 8 years now. Good luck in 2004!

2000_Gore_Bayh/questions_json/382@24/des: Where will you make the final stop(s) of your campaign before the voting begins?
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3312@0/descr: We need to expand benefits for Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid. We can use the surplus as well as defense cuts to balance these increases.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3345@1/descr: I can certainly see the need for some legislation, but it should be addressed at the state level.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3310@2/descr: We should enact tax cuts to return this money to the American people. My plan will reduce the burden for all Americans who currently pay income tax.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3311@3/descr: We should try to keep things as they are. The economy has been unusually good the past few years, and we already have a large federal debt to pay down.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3313@4/descr: I would prefer to see us allocate this money to new and existing government programs so that all Americans can share in our prosperity.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3314@5/descr: I believe that we need to return control of education to the states and to the people. I would end the Department of Education as President.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3315@6/descr: Many schools are squandering the resources of the federal government. I support providing school vouchers directly to parents, so that they can choose where their child goes.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3316@7/descr: We need more spending for America's struggling schools, and national standards and testing to identify and fix poor performers. Every child deserves a strong, functional school to attend.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3317@8/descr: We need to increase pay for teachers and increase funding for the Department of Education. I don't support nationwide standards or testing -- they will distort the learning process and lead to education by rote.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3318@9/descr: The Social Security system is a financial time bomb. We need to get rid of it, or at the very least cut its benefits significantly.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3319@10/desc: The average worker would do much better if their money was invested in the stock market. I support a plan to allow workers to contribute at least some of their Social Security contribution to an individual investment account.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3320@11/desc: I would establish an iron-clad lockbox for the Social Security fund. When we allow the federal government to borrow our Social Security money, we put every senior in this country at risk.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3321@12/desc: We need to increase benefits for Social Security. Many people can barely survive on the monthly payment, while we spend billions on the military and run a huge budget surplus.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3322@13/desc: The Cold War is over. We should cut defense spending and stop operating so many bases overseas. I would pull troops out of places like Germany and Okinawa, where we are no longer defending anything.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3323@14/desc: America should remain tough, but humble. I am concerned about some of our recent interventions in places like Somalia and Serbia.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3324@15/desc: We need to remain an engaged, committed defender of human rights in the world. We should do everything possible to secure the friendship of nations like Russia and China, and to prevent atrocities and genocide in the developing world.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3325@16/desc: I would focus on removing dictators like Saddam Hussein and Kim Jong Il from power. They threaten the stability of the world and perpetrate evil upon their people.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3326@17/desc: Bill Clinton was an embarrassment to the United States, and his impeachment was well-deserved. I believe that he should have been removed from office.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3327@18/desc: I don't think we need to belabor the point. I pledge to the American people that I will restore honor and dignity to the White House when I am President.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3328@19/desc: I am my own man. I respect Bill Clinton in many ways, but his personal conduct was lacking in this case.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3329@20/desc: This is a non-issue. Bill Clinton is one the best Presidents of the last fifty years, and we should be focusing on his policies and successes, not his personal affairs.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3330@21/desc: Returning Elian to Cuba was unconscionable. I did not support this decision by the Clinton Administration.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3331@22/desc: We should be talking less about Elian, and more about my plans to expand upon the great prosperity of this nation.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3332@23/desc: The law is the law. Elian belongs in Cuba with his father. These questions are never easy, but the Clinton Administration and Janet Reno did what they had to do.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3333@24/desc: This was an issue that had no bearing on the security of the United States. We also ruined any chance of mediation by insisting on the autonomy of Kosovo.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3334@25/desc: This certainly helped unseat Slobodan Milosevic, but as President I will make sure that America treads carefully before intervening in foreign nations' affairs.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3335@26/desc: I support our actions in this theatre. For minimal cost we were able to stop a potential genocide and put a dictator to justice.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3336@27/desc: The bombing of Serbia killed many innocent civilians and increased antagonism with Russia and China. I believe military intervention should be a last resort.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3337@28/desc: We need huge tax cuts across the board. Corporate, personal, and capital gains taxes should be slashed. This will further expand the economy through increases in investment.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3338@29/desc: My budget will cut taxes and return a portion of our budget surplus to the American people. Everybody who pays taxes will receive a reduction.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3339@30/desc: We have a plan for middle class tax cuts. But it would be irresponsible to make huge changes while we still have a large debt.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3340@31/desc: I have no plan to cut taxes. If anything, we might need some increases to strengthen Social Security.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3341@32/desc: I support a strong, overwhelming response against whoever perpetrated this attack. Any government that harbors such terrorists should be overthrown, even if it requires the commitment of American troops.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3342@33/desc: We need to do two things -- first of all we need better procedures to ensure that our forces in dangerous regions do better at protecting themselves. Secondly, we will investigate who is responsible for this attack, be it Al-Qaeda or some other group, and attack them accordingly.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3343@34/desc: This attack was a tragedy, but it underscores the need to the United States to have a more limited foreign policy. The Cold War is over, and it doesn't make sense to deploy troops in so many parts of the world.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3344@35/desc: A crime is a crime, no matter what the motive is. I do not support ideas that some victims should be held in higher regard than others.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3346@36/desc: I support increased federal hate crime legislation. No American should ever feel like a target of intimidation because of their identity.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3347@37/desc: I do not support new gun control laws. We need better enforcement of the existing laws we have. The Assault Weapons Ban should be allowed to expire.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3348@38/desc: I support the right to bear arms, with a couple of common-sense restrictions. We need background checks at gun shows, and better prevention measures to keep guns away from the mentally ill.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3349@39/desc: We need to renew the Assault Weapons Ban and make it permanent. I support other measures such as trigger locks to reduce gun violence in this country.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3350@40/desc: The only way we will end gun violence in this country is through large-scale legislation and the confiscation of troublesome weapons. The Second Amendment was never meant to apply to individuals.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3355@41/desc: We have no proof that global warming exists, and we should be expanding our production of coal and oil to obtain energy independence. I would not surrender the sovereignty of our nation for such trivial objectives.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3356@42/desc: I would not. The Protocol exempts 80% of the world, including major population centers such as China and India, from compliance, and would cause serious harm to the US economy.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3357@43/desc: It seems very unlikely that the Senate will ever come up with the votes to ratify this agreement. I don't know how my support or opposition would change that equation.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3358@44/desc: We have worked for years with many other countries to negotiate this agreement. I support the environment and believe the Protocol should be ratified.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3363@45/desc: I believe we haven't gone far enough on this issue. Saddam Hussein is a destabilizing leader, and he must be removed for the Middle East to truly prosper.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3364@46/desc: We are following the right course in Iraq. We must enforce our agreement to prevent Saddam from acquiring weapons of mass destruction. Saddam is allowing the sanctions to harm his people for his own selfish purposes.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3365@47/desc: The United States is much too entangled in the Middle East. We should pull back from the region and end sanctions in Iraq. I might remind people that these sanctions have killed hundreds of thousands of Iraqi children.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3374@48/desc: This seems like another attempt by the Clintons to stretch the rules. Hillary Clinton is clearly from Arkansas and should seek office from that state if she so desires.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3375@49/desc: I don't have any comment. I trust the people of New York to make the right decision on this issue.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3376@50/desc: Off the record, I am uncomfortable with this, but I prefer not to make a public statement about it.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3377@51/desc: The Clintons have added a greatly to the political life of the United States. I support Hillary Clinton in her campaign.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3378@52/desc: I see how this is appealing to some conservatives, but it still represents the interference of the federal government in education.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3379@53/desc: I strongly support this idea and will work to implement it as President. All parents deserve to choose where their child will attend school.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3380@54/desc: This plan will take money out of the public schools and will not fix the underlying problem of poor education in the United States.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3381@55/desc: Absolutely. Anything we can do to work towards energy independence in this country is a positive step. Oil and coal are the foundation of any energy policy, and should be exploited as much as possible.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3382@56/desc: This is fine with me, but it is a small part of the overall solution. We need to drill wherever we can, while encouraging innovation in other sectors of the energy market.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3383@57/desc: I oppose these plans. The ANWR is an environmental treasure of the United States, and the oil gained from any exploitation will be relatively limited.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3384@58/desc: This is a giveaway to oil companies that will not resolve America's underlying energy issues. We need more government investment in renewable energy sources, and strict regulations on oil and coal.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3388@59/desc: Absolutely. This is just another example of meddling that harms the economy, hurts energy production, and puts hard-working Americans out of work.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3389@60/desc: Unfortunately, coal is one of the dirtiest forms of energy in existence. I don't see how we can continue to rely on it for the majority of America's energy needs.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3397@61/desc: The Clinton Administration has added 23 million jobs to the American economy and unleashed an unprecedented wave of prosperity and innovation. I will continue his policies as President so that all Americans can prosper in the coming years.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3398@62/desc: We must not undo eight years of progress under President Clinton by cutting key programs and squandering the surplus on tax cuts for the rich. My opponent not only lacks experience, but his conservative ideas are out of step with those of the American public.
2000_Gore_Bayh/answers_json/3399@63/desc: I stand here tonight as my own man. We have much more work to do to ensure that America's prosperity flows to all of the people.
